pathway.title: Trinet Group, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Debt service capacity is strong and the maturity profile is clean, but the first test is the sequence of refinancing. Net debt of USD 568 million is 1.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 359 million, or USD 581 million and 1.62x pro forma for the October 2026 dividend, and cash interest cover is 7.33x. Both notes are fixed rate and senior unsecured, and the first maturity is USD 500 million in March 2029. The USD 700 million revolver has no borrowings but matures in August 2028, before those notes, so it must be extended or replaced to remain a backstop when the notes turn current; its maturity date is stated only in the 2024 annual report. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 126; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

Earnings are the weakest dimension because they are an insurance spread, not a service fee. Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 697 million in FY2023 to USD 425 million in FY2025, a fall of 39.02%, while the insurance cost ratio rose from 84% to 91%, and each point of that ratio is worth USD 42.24 million on FY2025 insurance service revenues. The ratio of 86% for the nine months to 2026-09-30 includes a one-time recovery of USD 21 million, the third quarter ratio was 89%, Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter was USD 89 million against USD 100 million a year earlier and the last-twelve-months ratio was 88.29%, so the recovery to USD 460 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is not yet a trend. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C16; calculation C04

Revenue durability is weak because the client base is shrinking and can leave on short notice. Total worksite employees were 10.99% below a year earlier at 2026-09-30, mainly in technology and professional services clients and partly because of health benefit repricing, and total revenues fell 4.86% in the nine months despite 8% higher monthly revenue per worksite employee. Clients can generally cancel on 30 days' notice, and five states account for about 64% of paid wages, which concentrates both revenue and insurance pricing. No client exceeded 10% of revenue in 2023 to 2025 and bad debt was USD 3 million a year, so the risk is broad attrition, not the loss of one large client. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 112; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

Cash conversion is good, but shareholder payments, not operations, decide whether leverage falls. Free cash flow was USD 234 million in FY2025 against shareholder payments of USD 235 million, and USD 243 million against USD 134 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, so payments took 100.43% of free cash flow in FY2025 and 55.14% in 2026. The board added USD 336 million of repurchase authority in February 2026 and USD 311 million remained at 2026-09-30, and the revolver's limits on payments to stockholders cannot be read, so the pace is a board choice that no readable term constrains. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C18

A material part of reported EBITDA is yield on client funds, and it is running off. Interest income was 19.76% of FY2025 reported EBITDA and 14.76% over the last twelve months, and it fell to USD 39 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 from USD 53 million because refund interest and average balances fell. Receivables from the IRS for employee retention credits fell from USD 831 million at FY2024 to USD 310 million at 2026-09-30, so part of the shrinking client balances is refunds being processed, not clients leaving, which qualifies the Financial foundation's reading of the fall as a shrinking funding float; the filings do not say how much. If the IRS finds claims ineligible, Trinet may seek reimbursement from clients, to whom a net USD 21 million had been distributed at 2026-09-30, but the annual report says the IRS holds professional employer organizations responsible for repaying rejected tax credits and a contract does not guarantee recovery from clients. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C14

Liquidity is adequate near term, with one exposure that a bad insurance year would call on twice. Unrestricted cash was USD 328 million at 2026-09-30, and pro forma cash after the October 2026 dividend is not established. The USD 700 million revolver was undrawn before letters of credit, while USD 299 million of carrier collateral sits in restricted funds and carriers may require it to be adjusted when facts change, and Trinet says it anticipates funding further collateral. A claims shock would therefore lower EBITDA and could also pull corporate cash into collateral. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 80; calculation C02

Governance risk is medium and rests on willingness, not on terms a creditor can read. In 2023 the company repurchased about USD 1,000 million of shares, USD 360 million of them from the largest stockholder, which holds about 38% and may nominate a director, using USD 600 million of new borrowings; since then the revolver has been repaid and buybacks have come from cash flow. The debt documents and the proxy statement were not supplied, so the limits on future payments and the board's independence are not established. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 115; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

Refinancing the 2029 notes will probably cost more but looks manageable. The notes carry 3.50%, and the pricing-service fair value of USD 467 million against USD 500 million of principal, 93.40% of principal, indicates a market yield above that coupon, while the 2031 notes fell from USD 414 million to USD 397 million of fair value against USD 400 million of principal. If the 2029 notes were refinanced at the coupon of the 2031 notes, cash interest cover would fall from 7.33x to 5.35x on last-twelve-months reported EBITDA; this is an assumption, not a market quote. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C11; calculation C12

cells.text: Co-employment PEO and administrative-services (ASO) provider of payroll, benefits, risk and compliance services to small and medium-size businesses
Professional service revenues (fee per worksite employee), insurance service revenues (benefit and workers' compensation billings) and interest income on funds held for clients
Fees and insurance rates are set in advance for the benefit period; monthly revenue per co-employed worksite employee rose 8% in 9M 2026
Insurance costs are the largest cost: USD 3,835 million of USD 4,793 million total costs and expenses in FY2025; operating expenses USD 902 million
Fully insured risk-based health and workers' compensation policies; the company reimburses claims within a deductible layer, up to USD 1 million per workers' compensation claim
PEO contracts renew annually and either party may cancel on 30 days' notice; ASO contracts are monthly or annual with 30 days' notice
Client changes peak in January and health claims costs rise later in the year; implied Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA was USD 57 million against USD 368 million in the first nine months
Clients prefund payroll, taxes and benefits two to three days before payroll dates; the funds are restricted and offset by matching liabilities
Capital expenditures including capitalized software were USD 69 million in FY2025 and USD 74 million in 9M 2026
Nearly all revenue is in the United States; five states account for about 64% of paid wages; a client service center operates in India
Management says it is resetting health benefit rates, expanding broker distribution and launching an AI assistant

runs.text: The strongest support is low, fixed-rate leverage with a distant first maturity. Net debt of USD 568 million is 1.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, or USD 581 million and 1.62x pro forma for the October 2026 dividend, all debt is two unsecured fixed-rate notes, and the first maturity is USD 500 million in March 2029. Rate rises do not lift interest cost while the revolver is undrawn, and an earnings shock has more than two years before a refinancing, which lowers the probability of default over that period. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A second support is cash conversion. Free cash flow was USD 286 million over the last twelve months after USD 49 million of cash interest, so debt service is covered comfortably and leverage can fall quickly if buybacks slow, which supports deleveraging capacity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

A third support is that client money does not fund the company. Clients prefund payroll and related taxes, and the USD 941 million of payroll funds collected and USD 40 million held in the trust for administrative services users at 2026-09-30 are restricted and matched by liabilities to clients and tax authorities, so working capital does not draw on corporate cash and the USD 328 million of unrestricted cash is available for debt service; pro forma cash after the October 2026 dividend is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 35; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

A fourth support is a simpler structure. The revolver was repaid in 2024 and 2025, the two notes are the only debt, and the 2023 debt-funded repurchase has not been repeated, which removes floating-rate exposure and leaves the next test to 2028 and 2029. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 119; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The weakest dimension is earnings stability. Adjusted EBITDA fell USD 272 million from FY2023 to FY2025 as the insurance cost ratio rose from 84% to 91%, and each point is worth USD 42.24 million, so a return to the FY2025 ratio would remove USD 111 million, or 30.92%, of last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, and fees fixed in advance leave no time to react. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 74; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C16

A second weakness is a shrinking client base with short contracts. Total worksite employees were 10.99% lower year on year, clients can cancel on 30 days' notice, and the repricing that lifts margin contributed to the losses, so revenue has to be won back at the same time as margin is defended. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

A third weakness is that shareholder payments absorb free cash flow at the board's discretion. Payments of USD 235 million matched free cash flow of USD 234 million in FY2025, the largest stockholder holds about 38%, and the limits in the debt documents are not readable, so leverage is a policy variable, not a result. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C18

A fourth weakness is that part of EBITDA is yield on client funds. Interest income was 19.76% of FY2025 reported EBITDA and fell to USD 39 million from USD 53 million in nine months, so lower client balances or short-term rates reduce EBITDA without any change in operations. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 27; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

runs.text: The only acquisition in the period is Cocoon Financial Services, a leave-management software company, bought for cash in the second quarter of 2026 with a total price of USD 23 million, USD 22 million net of the target's own cash. It added goodwill of USD 4 million and acquired technology of USD 17 million, no pro forma results were given as the effect is not material, and the reports differ on the closing day. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 42

No new debt was issued in 2025 or in the nine months of 2026. The most recent issues are the USD 400 million 2031 notes of August 2023, whose proceeds funded a tender offer and a private repurchase from the largest stockholder, and the USD 500 million 2029 notes of February 2021. The revolver was increased from USD 500 million to USD 700 million and extended to August 2028 in August 2023, and its last borrowings were repaid in July 2025. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source readiness for Trinet Group, Inc. (tnet-937098) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the five supplied filings can support the financial foundation, business and governance and fundamental credit work selected for this run, and what the filings cannot support. No ratings, quotes, deal terms, peer set, portfolio or executed legal documents were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the dates on each report's signature page; the 2025 annual report (filed 2026-02-12) and the June 2026 quarterly report (filed 2026-07-30) are also confirmed by the September 2026 quarterly report. No earlier analyses were supplied and no external sources were used. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five filings support the financial foundation, business profile and fundamental credit work selected for this run, but not covenant headroom, note pricing, rating triggers or recovery, so creditor protection beyond reported covenant compliance cannot be judged from them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The evidence is one reporting entity current to 2026-09-30: debt of USD 896 million on the balance sheet against USD 900 million of note principal, unrestricted cash of USD 328 million and a USD 700 million revolver with no borrowings outstanding. The covenant level, revolver availability after letters of credit, ratings, quotes, guarantor names and the executed debt documents are not in the set, and each limits only the conclusion that depends on it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C02; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The set is one reporting entity across five primary filings: the annual reports for 2024 and 2025 and the quarterly reports for March, June and September 2026. The newest was signed 20 days before the cutoff, so events between 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-18 are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The statements support a financial foundation: audited annual statements for 2023 to 2025, and for 2026 the first quarter, six months and nine months, each with income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and a reconciliation of net income to adjusted earnings. The 2025 interim periods exist only as comparatives inside the 2026 reports, so discrete 2025 quarters are not available as filed, and the quarterly worksite-employee charts in the annual report carry no figures in the text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt instruments are identifiable: a USD 500 million senior unsecured note due March 2029, a USD 400 million senior unsecured note due August 2031, and a USD 700 million revolver with no borrowings outstanding since July 2025. None of the three facilities matures within twelve months of the cutoff, but the revolver maturity of August 2028 is stated only in the 2024 annual report. Rates, effective rates and issuance costs are printed only in the annual report. The quarterly reports give principal and the balance-sheet figure of USD 896 million but no instrument table, and the principal of USD 900 million exceeds that figure by USD 4 million without a printed explanation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 118–119; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C02; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Corporate liquidity can be built from the filings: unrestricted cash was USD 328 million at 2026-09-30, and the filings separate it from payroll and insurance-collateral funds that are restricted. The undrawn amount of the revolver after letters of credit is stated only at year-end, USD 699 million of USD 700 million at 2025-12-31, so the September 2026 amount is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt are identifiable and sit outside the debt figure: operating lease liabilities of USD 47 million at 2025-12-31, purchase obligations of USD 136 million, workers' compensation obligations of USD 151 million, and the payroll and tax liabilities held for worksite employees, which the filings show offset by matching client-related current assets. No pension, retiree medical, factoring, supply-chain finance or consent decree obligation is described, and litigation is accrued at amounts the filings call immaterial.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The revolver carries a financial covenant on maximum total net leverage, and compliance is stated at every period end supplied. The maximum level, any step-down, the definition and the reported ratio are not printed, so headroom is not calculable. The restrictions in the note indentures on liens, subsidiary guarantees and mergers are described only in summary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The run settings supply no ratings, quotes, deal terms, peer set, portfolio, management bridge or executed debt documents, and the filings name no rating of the issuer. Ratings & triggers, Peer benchmark, Security selection, Legal & covenants and Recovery & fulcrum therefore have no evidence in this set, and Market-implied risk has only the pricing-service fair values of the two notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership evidence is partial: the largest stockholder, an investment firm affiliated with Atairos, held about 38% at 2026-01-31 and keeps a board nomination right while it holds at least 15%, but directors, officers and compensation sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a ready-with-limitations verdict is that the missing items sit exactly where a creditor needs precision: the leverage covenant is the one maintenance test the filings mention, and the revolver is the one committed bank facility they describe. Supplying the credit agreement and indentures would let covenant headroom, availability after letters of credit, guarantee status and lien limits be tested, and Legal & covenants and Covenant capacity could move out of blocked. A filing, release or rating action dated between 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-18 could also change the view, because a later financing, amendment or acquisition would sit outside every figure in this set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Consistent compliance statements in all five filings, and no revolver borrowings since July 2025, point the other way: they suggest the missing covenant level matters less to the selected modules than to a covenant or recovery analysis. They do not replace the level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The verdicts rest on filing text only. Tables are flattened into lines, charts are not retained as figures, and a page reference in this work is a text chunk, not a printed page. Absent items are never treated as zero: the 2025 interim filings as filed, the covenant level, letters of credit at 2026-09-30, the proxy statement, every guarantor name, any filing after 2026-10-29 and every external input. The revolver maturity is stated only in the 2024 annual report. The Cocoon closing day and the 2023 adjusted EBITDA margin differ between filings and are preserved, not reconciled. File integrity and text extraction were verified before this module ran, and no result is recorded here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All amounts are as printed in USD millions unless stated. The rows record the arithmetic used in the findings; nothing here is a credit metric.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: The maximum total net leverage ratio, any step-down, the definition and the issuer's reported ratio are not printed in any of the five filings, which state only that the company was in compliance. Covenant headroom is therefore not calculable; the credit agreement or a compliance certificate would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: The 2021 credit agreement and its amendments, the 2021 and 2023 indentures and the two 2025 supplemental indentures are listed as exhibits but were not supplied. Redemption prices after the call dates, lien and guarantee limits, events of default and security cannot be read from the documents themselves.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: The guarantors of the two note issues are not named, the exhibit list names TriNet USA, Inc. as Holdings under the credit agreement and refers to a separate borrower it does not name, and no obligor, restricted-group or subsidiary financials are supplied. The two supplemental indentures dated March 2025 list only the company and the trustee as parties, and the filings do not say what they changed, so guarantee status is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: Revolver availability after letters of credit is stated only at year-end, USD 699 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 606 million at 2024-12-31, and the 2024 annual report says letters of credit reduce availability. The amount at 2026-09-30 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: The run settings supply no ratings, quotes, deal terms, peer set, portfolio, management bridge, prior case or executed legal documents, and the filings give no rating of the issuer. Ratings & triggers, Peer benchmark, Security selection, Legal & covenants and Recovery & fulcrum have no evidence in this set; Market-implied risk has only pricing-service fair values of the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: Nothing dated after 2026-10-29 was supplied: no earnings release, current report, rating action or market price. Events up to the cutoff are not established beyond the October dividend recorded in the latest quarterly report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The proxy statement incorporated by reference into the annual report was not supplied, so directors, officers, compensation and the beneficial ownership table are not established; Atairos's holding is taken from a risk factor as at 2026-01-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The revolver maturity of 2028-08-16 is stated only in the 2024 annual report. The 2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports describe the revolver without restating the date, and the glossary shows no amendment later than August 2023, so the date is carried forward but not reconfirmed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The first quarter report gives April 8, 2026 as the closing day of the Cocoon acquisition and the second and third quarter reports give April 10, 2026. The later reports control and the difference is kept, not reconciled; the price of USD 23 million, USD 22 million net of cash acquired, agrees across them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The 2024 annual report prints the 2023 adjusted EBITDA margin as 14.2% and the 2025 annual report prints 14.0% for the same Adjusted EBITDA of USD 697 million. The amount agrees; the margin is recomputed from printed revenue and the earlier denominator is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied, so discrete 2025 quarters exist only as comparatives inside the 2026 reports, which say some prior-year amounts were reclassified. The quarterly worksite-employee charts in the annual report carry no figures in the extracted text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Trinet Group, Inc. (tnet-937098) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated income statement, cash flow, balance sheet, debt, liquidity and credit metrics for FY2023 to FY2025, nine months 2025 and nine months 2026, with a last-twelve-months view to 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the dates on each report's signature page. No external sources were used. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trinet's leverage is moderate and well covered but sits on a shrinking, interest-income-supported earnings base: net debt is 1.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, cash interest cover is 7.33x and no borrowed debt matures before 2029, so debt service looks secure while earnings durability is the exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C09; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA of USD 359 million is derived, because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA of USD 460 million, and interest income on client funds supplies USD 53 million of it. Net debt of USD 568 million becomes USD 581 million, or 1.62x, after the October dividend. The covenant level and revolver availability after letters of credit are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C02; calculation C07; calculation C11; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage rose from FY2023 to FY2025 because earnings fell, not because debt rose, and has partly reversed in 2026: total debt fell from USD 1,093 million at FY2023 to USD 896 million at 2026-09-30, but reported EBITDA fell from USD 613 million in FY2023 to USD 339 million in FY2025 before recovering to USD 359 million on a last-twelve-months basis. Net debt over reported EBITDA moved from 1.31x to 1.72x, 1.79x and 1.58x, and on Adjusted EBITDA from 1.16x to 1.23x. Net debt counts unrestricted cash only, so the USD 50 million of corporate investments at 2026-09-30 would lower net leverage to 1.44x if included.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover has fallen from the FY2023 level because the first coupon on the 2031 notes was paid in February 2024, after that year-end: reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 24.52x in FY2023, 6.15x in FY2024, 6.52x in FY2025 and 7.33x on a last-twelve-months basis (9.39x on Adjusted EBITDA). Cash interest paid was USD 52 million in FY2025 and USD 49 million over the last twelve months, which compares with interest expense, bank fees and other of USD 56 million in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C03; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is solid but is returned to shareholders in full: operating cash flow was USD 303 million in FY2025 and free cash flow after capital expenditure USD 234 million, against buybacks and dividends of USD 235 million. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 free cash flow was USD 243 million against USD 134 million of buybacks and dividends, so the 2026 pace leaves room to build cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is ample against a maturity profile with nothing borrowed due before 2029: unrestricted cash was USD 328 million and the USD 700 million revolver had no borrowings at 2026-09-30, while the only maturities are USD 500 million in 2029 and USD 400 million in 2031 and the revolver itself matures in 2028. Availability after letters of credit is stated only at year-end, USD 699 million at 2025-12-31, so the September figure is before letters of credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are identifiable: operating lease liabilities of USD 67 million at 2026-09-30, purchase obligations of USD 136 million and workers' compensation obligations of USD 151 million at FY2025, none of which is added to debt. No pension, retiree medical, factoring, supply-chain finance or consent decree obligation is described, and litigation is accrued at amounts the filings call immaterial.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The latest quarter was weaker than the nine months suggest: in Q3 2026 revenue was USD 1,175 million against USD 1,232 million, derived reported EBITDA USD 68 million against USD 79 million, Adjusted EBITDA USD 89 million against USD 100 million and net income USD 31 million against USD 34 million. The nine-month gain in Adjusted EBITDA includes a one-time recovery of USD 21 million of prior-year costs in Q2 2026, so the underlying trend is flatter than the nine-month comparison. No debt was issued or repaid in the nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Part of reported EBITDA is yield on client funds, not operations. Interest income earned on funds held for clients is booked in revenue and was USD 67 million in FY2025, or 19.76% of reported EBITDA, and USD 53 million over the last twelve months, or 14.76%. The funding float behind it is shrinking: payroll tax liabilities and other payroll withholdings fell from USD 1,906 million at FY2024 to USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30, and nine-month interest income fell from USD 53 million to USD 39 million. Lower client balances or lower short-term rates cut EBITDA without any change in operating performance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One subsequent event is stated: the October 2026 dividend, which was declared and unpaid at 2026-09-30 at USD 13 million. It raises net debt to USD 581 million and net leverage to 1.62x on the same reported EBITDA, and it is kept out of the period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Data quality limits the foundation in three ways. The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from income before tax, interest expense, bank fees and other, and amortization of intangible assets. The quarterly reports print no debt table, so USD 900 million of note principal exceeds balance-sheet debt of USD 896 million by USD 4 million without a printed explanation. Source dashes are carried as not supplied, not as zero.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C01; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the earnings-durability concern is nine-month momentum: Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 403 million against USD 368 million a year earlier, operating cash flow rose to USD 317 million from USD 242 million, the insurance cost ratio fell to 86% from 90%, and net leverage on reported EBITDA improved from 1.79x at FY2025 to 1.58x. Implied Q4 2025 reported EBITDA was only USD 31 million, so a Q4 2026 above that level lifts the last-twelve-months figure. That case is weaker than it looks, because the nine-month gain includes the one-time recovery and the latest quarter went the other way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C22; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: What would change the view is a reversal in the drivers of that improvement: a higher insurance cost ratio, a further fall in worksite employees (total worksite employees were down 11% year on year at 2026-09-30), lower interest income as client balances or rates fall, or shareholder payments above free cash flow as in FY2025. A covenant level or letters-of-credit figure that proved tight would also change it, and neither is in the sources.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.value: Reported EBITDA is a derived figure and the interim tables use a last-twelve-months construction, so neither ties to a printed statement line for interim periods. Debt detail by instrument is printed only at year-end, revolver availability after letters of credit is stated only at year-end, the covenant level is not printed, and discrete 2025 quarters are available only as comparatives inside the 2026 reports. Dashes in the statements are not assumed to be zero, and the October dividend is linked to the declared-and-unpaid amount by inference.

fields.value: - High: The maximum total net leverage ratio, any step-down, the definition and the reported ratio are not printed in any of the five filings, so covenant headroom is not calculable. It restricts any covenant conclusion; the credit agreement or a compliance certificate would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: Revolver availability after letters of credit is stated only at year-end, USD 606 million at 2024-12-31 and USD 699 million at 2025-12-31, and is not stated at 2026-09-30 or 2023-12-31. The liquidity table therefore shows the commitment less borrowings at 2026-09-30, which is before letters of credit, and no figure for 2023-12-31. Letters of credit outstanding would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from income before tax, interest expense, bank fees and other, and amortization of intangible assets. fields.value: - Medium: The statements print dashes that are carried as not supplied, not as zero: accounts receivable in FY2025, other payroll assets in FY2025, accounts payable and other liabilities in FY2024 and 9M 2025, workers' compensation in 9M 2025, proceeds from sale of business in three periods, other investments in two years, the 2031 note proceeds and revolver proceeds outside FY2023, dividends in FY2023, revolver repayment in 9M 2026, investments in FY2024 and FY2025, and the transaction and integration costs and restructuring lines. Operating cash flow still equals the printed adjustments and movements in every period, and the 2024 annual report's two payables lines net to zero for FY2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied, so discrete 2025 quarters and a balance sheet at 2025-09-30 are not available as filed, the 2026 reports say some prior-year amounts were reclassified, and no maintenance or growth capital expenditure split is printed.

fields.value: - Low: The company reports one segment, so no segment revenue or elimination schedule exists; revenue is shown by service type, and no segment sum is stated.

fields.value: - Low: The first quarter report gives April 8, 2026 as the closing day of the Cocoon acquisition and the later reports give April 10, 2026; the cash price of USD 22 million net of cash acquired is in the 9M 2026 investing flows and the day does not change any figure here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The 2024 annual report prints the FY2023 Adjusted EBITDA margin as 14.2% and the 2025 annual report prints 14.0% for the same USD 697 million; the margin used here is recomputed from printed revenue.

fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction facts for Trinet Group, Inc. (tnet-937098) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is what the issuer does, who controls it, how it has treated creditors through capital allocation, and which transactions and events matter to a creditor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the dates on each report's signature page. No external sources were used. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trinet is a co-employment HR outsourcer that earns an insurance spread on a shrinking client base, with a concentrated largest stockholder and a 2023 debt-funded buyback, so creditor governance risk is medium and rests on board discretion, not on terms we can read.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Insurance service revenues were 84.31% of FY2025 revenue, and had the insurance cost ratio stayed at its FY2023 level, FY2025 insurance costs would have been USD 273.09 million lower, close to the USD 272 million fall in Adjusted EBITDA since FY2023. Shareholder payments of USD 235 million in FY2025 equalled free cash flow of USD 234 million. Legal capacity to distribute more is not established because the debt documents were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C11; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are an insurance-underwriting spread, so claims costs, not service fees, decide creditor cash flow. Insurance service revenues were USD 4,224 million in FY2025 against insurance costs of USD 3,835 million, and fees are set in advance, so each percentage point of the insurance cost ratio is worth USD 42.24 million of earnings. The ratio rose from 84% in FY2023 to 91% in FY2025 and was 86% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, helped by repricing and a one-time USD 21 million recovery of prior-year costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C08; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The client base is shrinking and can leave quickly, so revenue visibility is short. Total worksite employees at 2026-09-30 were 10.99% below a year earlier, mainly in technology and professional services clients and partly because of health benefit repricing. PEO clients may cancel on 30 days' notice, and five states account for about 64% of paid wages, which also concentrates insurance pricing. Revenue per co-employed worksite employee rose 8%, which has so far only partly offset lost volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Client funds give the business liquidity and a yield but also a contingent exposure. Clients prefund payroll, payroll taxes and benefits, which are held as restricted funds, and interest on those funds was USD 67 million of FY2025 revenue, partly from interest on payroll tax refunds. In nine months 2026 interest income was USD 39 million against USD 53 million, because of lower refund interest and lower average cash balances. In some states a PEO must pay wages and taxes even when a client has not remitted, so the prefunding discipline is a creditor protection worth monitoring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium because the one documented extraction-style act is old and the current pattern is cash-funded, while capacity is unreadable. The largest stockholder, an affiliate of Atairos, held about 38% at 2026-01-31, may nominate a director while it holds 15% or more, and with directors and officers controls about 39%. In 2023 the company bought USD 360 million of shares from Atairos and USD 640 million through a tender offer, funded with USD 400 million of 2031 notes and a USD 200 million revolver draw, which lifted debt by USD 597 million in a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 74; calculation C07; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Current capital allocation is funded from cash and returned all of free cash flow in FY2025. Buybacks and dividends were USD 235 million against free cash flow of USD 234 million that year, and USD 134 million against USD 243 million in the nine months of 2026. The board added USD 336 million of repurchase authority in February 2026, USD 311 million remained at 2026-09-30, and the dividend has risen from USD 0.25 to USD 0.29 per share. The revolver's negative covenants restrict payments to stockholders, but their size is not readable, so willingness is evidenced and capacity is not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring of earnings but not of covenants. The 2025 financial statements and internal controls received unqualified audit opinions, with a critical audit matter on accrued workers' compensation and health insurance costs, which are judgemental estimates. The chief financial officer changed under agreements dated in October 2025, the reason is not stated, and the proxy statement with director and pay detail was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition appetite is not established as a pattern: the 2022 acquisitions of subsidiaries, including Zenefits, cost USD 229 million of net cash and the 2026 Cocoon purchase USD 22 million, with a restructuring that wound down the software-only HRIS product in between, so two deals in five years of different size show no consistent funding or integration behavior.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 129; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for lower risk is that the 2023 episode has been unwound in substance: the revolver was repaid in full by July 2025 with USD 110 million in 2024 and USD 90 million in 2025, all remaining debt is two fixed-rate notes, no sponsor fees or related-party leakage are stated, related-party revenue is USD 4 million, and buybacks since then came from cash flow. A medium level would fall to low if the debt documents showed tight limits on distributions, and would rise to high if another debt-funded repurchase, a large special dividend or a stockholder fee appeared, or if the largest stockholder sold or bought a block.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 88

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so the board's composition, pay design and the beneficial ownership table are not established; this keeps the governance level at medium on documented behavior and prevents a view on board independence from creditors' standpoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so what the documents let the company pay out or invest is unknown; the willingness conclusion therefore cannot be tested against capacity, and the level stays medium instead of moving either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue by vertical and by client size is not disclosed, so the shrinking-client-base conclusion rests on worksite employee counts and the five-state concentration alone and cannot say whether attrition is broad or concentrated in a few large accounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The reasons for the October 2025 chief financial officer transition and the vintage and remaining life of Atairos' investment vehicle are not stated, so no conclusion on management continuity or exit pressure is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only acquisition in the period is Cocoon Financial Services, a leave-management software company, bought for cash in the second quarter of 2026 with a total price of USD 23 million, USD 22 million net of the target's own cash. It added goodwill of USD 4 million and acquired technology of USD 17 million, no pro forma results were given as the effect is not material, and the reports differ on the closing day.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was issued in 2025 or in the nine months of 2026. The most recent issues are the USD 400 million 2031 notes of August 2023, whose proceeds funded a tender offer and a private repurchase from the largest stockholder, and the USD 500 million 2029 notes of February 2021. The revolver was increased from USD 500 million to USD 700 million and extended to August 2028 in August 2023, and its last borrowings were repaid in July 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by the 2023 debt-funded repurchase and by distributions equal to free cash flow, because they added leverage and absorb deleveraging capacity, which implies refinancing and monitoring risk; countervailing evidence is the repaid revolver, cash-funded buybacks since, no stockholder fees and unqualified audit opinions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Trinet presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behavior is a debt-funded repurchase of USD 1,000 million in 2023, including USD 360 million bought from the largest stockholder, which matters because it raised leverage and set the 2031 maturity and implies that the board will lever for repurchases when it judges the price right. Countervailing evidence is a repaid revolver, buybacks funded from cash flow since, no stockholder fees stated and clean audit opinions. Further analysis requires the credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement. Governance review completed with limitations; the risk level is medium and the key gaps are the debt documents and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Trinet Group, Inc. (tnet-937098) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the overall fundamental credit profile built from the five supplied filings and the earlier Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance work: the strongest support, the weakest dimension, the primary downside path and what to monitor. No rating, security recommendation, covenant, recovery or sizing conclusion is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the dates on each report's signature page. No external sources were used. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trinet is adequate for creditors near term but exposed on earnings: debt service is well covered and nothing borrowed matures before 2029, yet earnings are an insurance spread on a shrinking client base, so repayment depends on claims discipline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 568 million was 1.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, and USD 581 million or 1.62x pro forma for the October 2026 dividend, with cash interest cover of 7.33x. Free cash flow equalled shareholder payments in FY2025, so net debt falls only while buybacks stay below free cash flow. Covenant headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service capacity is strong and the maturity profile is clean, but the first test is the sequence of refinancing. Net debt of USD 568 million is 1.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 359 million, or USD 581 million and 1.62x pro forma for the October 2026 dividend, and cash interest cover is 7.33x. Both notes are fixed rate and senior unsecured, and the first maturity is USD 500 million in March 2029. The USD 700 million revolver has no borrowings but matures in August 2028, before those notes, so it must be extended or replaced to remain a backstop when the notes turn current; its maturity date is stated only in the 2024 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 126; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are the weakest dimension because they are an insurance spread, not a service fee. Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 697 million in FY2023 to USD 425 million in FY2025, a fall of 39.02%, while the insurance cost ratio rose from 84% to 91%, and each point of that ratio is worth USD 42.24 million on FY2025 insurance service revenues. The ratio of 86% for the nine months to 2026-09-30 includes a one-time recovery of USD 21 million, the third quarter ratio was 89%, Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter was USD 89 million against USD 100 million a year earlier and the last-twelve-months ratio was 88.29%, so the recovery to USD 460 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is not yet a trend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C16; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is weak because the client base is shrinking and can leave on short notice. Total worksite employees were 10.99% below a year earlier at 2026-09-30, mainly in technology and professional services clients and partly because of health benefit repricing, and total revenues fell 4.86% in the nine months despite 8% higher monthly revenue per worksite employee. Clients can generally cancel on 30 days' notice, and five states account for about 64% of paid wages, which concentrates both revenue and insurance pricing. No client exceeded 10% of revenue in 2023 to 2025 and bad debt was USD 3 million a year, so the risk is broad attrition, not the loss of one large client.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 112; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is good, but shareholder payments, not operations, decide whether leverage falls. Free cash flow was USD 234 million in FY2025 against shareholder payments of USD 235 million, and USD 243 million against USD 134 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, so payments took 100.43% of free cash flow in FY2025 and 55.14% in 2026. The board added USD 336 million of repurchase authority in February 2026 and USD 311 million remained at 2026-09-30, and the revolver's limits on payments to stockholders cannot be read, so the pace is a board choice that no readable term constrains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A material part of reported EBITDA is yield on client funds, and it is running off. Interest income was 19.76% of FY2025 reported EBITDA and 14.76% over the last twelve months, and it fell to USD 39 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 from USD 53 million because refund interest and average balances fell. Receivables from the IRS for employee retention credits fell from USD 831 million at FY2024 to USD 310 million at 2026-09-30, so part of the shrinking client balances is refunds being processed, not clients leaving, which qualifies the Financial foundation's reading of the fall as a shrinking funding float; the filings do not say how much. If the IRS finds claims ineligible, Trinet may seek reimbursement from clients, to whom a net USD 21 million had been distributed at 2026-09-30, but the annual report says the IRS holds professional employer organizations responsible for repaying rejected tax credits and a contract does not guarantee recovery from clients.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate near term, with one exposure that a bad insurance year would call on twice. Unrestricted cash was USD 328 million at 2026-09-30, and pro forma cash after the October 2026 dividend is not established. The USD 700 million revolver was undrawn before letters of credit, while USD 299 million of carrier collateral sits in restricted funds and carriers may require it to be adjusted when facts change, and Trinet says it anticipates funding further collateral. A claims shock would therefore lower EBITDA and could also pull corporate cash into collateral.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 80; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium and rests on willingness, not on terms a creditor can read. In 2023 the company repurchased about USD 1,000 million of shares, USD 360 million of them from the largest stockholder, which holds about 38% and may nominate a director, using USD 600 million of new borrowings; since then the revolver has been repaid and buybacks have come from cash flow. The debt documents and the proxy statement were not supplied, so the limits on future payments and the board's independence are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-K_2024-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 115; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing the 2029 notes will probably cost more but looks manageable. The notes carry 3.50%, and the pricing-service fair value of USD 467 million against USD 500 million of principal, 93.40% of principal, indicates a market yield above that coupon, while the 2031 notes fell from USD 414 million to USD 397 million of fair value against USD 400 million of principal. If the 2029 notes were refinanced at the coupon of the 2031 notes, cash interest cover would fall from 7.33x to 5.35x on last-twelve-months reported EBITDA; this is an assumption, not a market quote.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the earnings concern is the 2026 recovery: nine-month operating cash flow was USD 317 million against USD 242 million, the insurance cost ratio was 86% against 90%, management calls the reset of health benefit rates substantially complete, and net debt was 1.58x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA against 1.79x at FY2025, with USD 581 million and 1.62x pro forma for the October 2026 dividend. If the ratio holds between 86% and 89% for four more quarters while worksite employees stabilise, earnings stability would move from weak to average and leverage would fall without a change in policy. The case is weaker than it looks: the nine-month ratio includes the USD 21 million one-time recovery, the third quarter ratio was 89%, USD 43 million of the USD 75 million rise in operating cash flow came from smaller working-capital outflows that can reverse, and the client base was still 10.99% smaller than a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tnet.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would weaken if the insurance cost ratio returned to the FY2025 level of 91% from the 88.29% implied for the last twelve months: that is worth USD 111 million, or 30.92% of last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, and would take net leverage to 2.29x, or 2.34x on USD 581 million pro forma for the October 2026 dividend, and cash interest cover to 5.06x before any repricing offset. It would also weaken if shareholder payments exceeded free cash flow again, if carrier collateral rose above USD 299 million, if the revolver were drawn, or if another debt-funded repurchase appeared. It would strengthen if the debt documents showed tight limits on payments to stockholders, or if the covenant level and letters of credit showed wide headroom.
